summary: Shozen Kumoi (1915–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. His career included posts at Otani, Bukkyo, and Kyoto universities.
Shri Krishna Saksena (b. 1897) worked in philosophy and Indology. Over his career, he served as a professor at both the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi.
Shri Krishna Sharma was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Beyond his academic work, which included teaching Dieter Schuh, he founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (b. 1859) was an Indology scholar. He served at Deccan College as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit starting in 1884, and later held Sanskrit professorships at Elphinstone College and Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shrikant S. Bahulkar works in Indology and Buddhist studies. A former student of Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, he has held posts as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth and BORI.

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar (1881–1967) was an Indologist and philosopher. After studying under Kashinath Bapu Pathak, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1937) and held secretarial roles at BORI and the All-India Oriental Conference.

Shrivatsa Goswami (b. 1950) works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied and taught at Banaras Hindu University, founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana in 1972, and held posts at Harvard's CSWR and the Vrindaban Research Institute.

Shu-Fen Chen is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock, later becoming a professor at National Tsing Hua University.

Shu-chen Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she was a teaching assistant in 1996 and studied under Jeffrey Hopkins, Karen C. Lang, Bradley W. Reed, and Ronald G. Dimberg.

Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar. He served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and held a post in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii (b. 1943) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his degrees from Komazawa University, studying under Shigeo Kamata, and spent his career there progressing from assistant (1971) to professor (1984, 2014).

Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Educated in China and France, he taught at Zhejiang University and the Central Academy of Fine Arts before serving as long-time director and honorary director of Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato (1919–2008) worked in Japanology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo and University of Paris, he held posts at Tokyo, UBC, Free University of Berlin, Sophia University, and Ritsumeikan University.
Shuichi Maida (1906–1967) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was educated at Kyoto University and studied under Haya Akegarasu.

Shuichi Nara (b. 1961) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. Educated at Keio University, he has served as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and a lecturer at Chuo University.
Shuji Takayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held research and teaching posts at Ryukoku University, Bukkyo University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Musashino University.

Shujiro Shimada (1907–1994) worked in Japanology, Sinology, and art history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1928 to 1931 and served on the faculty at Princeton University from ~1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and at Kyoto University, later serving as Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University.

Shuken Ito (b. 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed all of his higher education at Komazawa University, where he subsequently spent his academic career advancing from research assistant in the 1970s to full professor in 1991.
Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi and earned a PhD at Northwestern University under the supervision of Brook Ziporyn.
